topics.name: James: overview
topics.description: James is a letter from James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, with practical teaching on trials, living faith, the tongue, humility, wealth and patience.
evidence: Name the main themes of James in order
Say who the letter is from and to whom it is written
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what James tells believers to do with trials, words and wealth?

topics.name: Trials, wisdom and the crown of life
topics.description: James says to count trials as joy because tested faith produces patience, to ask God for wisdom without wavering, and promises the crown of life to the one who endures.
evidence: Explain what testing of faith produces
Say how James tells believers to ask for wisdom
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why James says to count it all joy when trials come?

topics.name: Temptation, the word and doing it
topics.description: James says God does not tempt anyone; desire gives birth to sin and sin to death, while every good gift comes from the Father of lights who gave new birth by the word of truth, and believers must be doers of the word.
evidence: Describe the path from desire to death in 1:14-15
Contrast hearing the word with doing it
State what James calls pure religion
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between hearing the word and doing it?

topics.name: No partiality: the royal law
topics.description: James rebukes giving the rich seats of honour and shaming the poor in the assembly, reminds them God chose the poor rich in faith, and calls loving your neighbour the royal law.
evidence: Describe the example of partiality in the assembly
Say what James calls the royal law
Explain why partiality is sin according to 2:9
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what James says is wrong with favouring the rich over the poor?

topics.name: Faith and works
topics.description: James argues that faith without works is dead, using the demons who believe, Abraham offering Isaac, and Rahab, and concludes a man is justified by works and not by faith only.
evidence: Explain what James means by faith that is alone and dead
Retell how Abraham and Rahab are used as examples
Compare the wording of James 2:24 with Romans 3:28 and 4:2-3
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what James is arguing about the kind of faith that is dead?

topics.name: The tongue
topics.description: James warns that few should be teachers, compares the tongue to a bit, a rudder and a fire, and says it cannot be tamed by man yet is used both to bless God and curse people.
evidence: Name the three pictures James uses for the tongue
Say what inconsistency James points out in 3:9-10
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say why James calls the tongue a fire?

topics.name: Wisdom from above and earthly wisdom
topics.description: James contrasts envy and strife, which he calls earthly, sensual and devilish wisdom, with wisdom from above, which is pure, peaceable, gentle and full of mercy and good fruits.
evidence: List the marks of wisdom from above
Describe what comes with bitter envying and strife
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how to tell wisdom from above from earthly wisdom?

topics.name: Conflicts, the world and humbling before God
topics.description: James traces fightings to desires within, calls friendship with the world enmity with God, and says God gives grace to the humble, so believers must submit, resist the devil and draw near to God.
evidence: Say where James says wars and fightings come from
List the commands in 4:7-10
Explain what God does with the proud and the humble
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what James says to do instead of fighting and loving the world?

topics.name: Judging others and boasting about tomorrow
topics.description: James forbids speaking evil of a brother and judging him since there is one lawgiver, and rebukes plans made without saying if the Lord will, since life is a vapour.
evidence: Say why James says there is one lawgiver
Explain what James says we should say about our plans
State the point of 4:17
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why James says to say, If the Lord will?

topics.name: Warning to the rich who defraud
topics.description: James tells rich men to weep for coming miseries: their riches are corrupted, wages withheld from labourers cry out to the Lord of sabaoth, and they have lived in luxury and condemned the just.
evidence: Name the charges James brings against the rich in 5:1-6
Say who hears the cries of the harvest labourers
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what the rich are accused of in James 5:1-6?

topics.name: Patience until the coming of the Lord
topics.description: James urges patience like the farmer waiting for rain, points to the prophets and Job as examples, says the Lord is pitiful and merciful, and tells them not to swear oaths.
evidence: Describe the farmer picture of patience
Name the examples of endurance James gives
Say what James tells them about oaths
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why James says to be patient until the coming of the Lord?

topics.name: Prayer, healing and restoring the wanderer
topics.description: James tells the afflicted to pray, the sick to call the elders, believers to confess faults and pray for one another, cites Elijah as a man like us whose prayer was answered, and ends by urging restoring one who strays from the truth.
evidence: Describe what the sick are told to do in 5:14-15
Say how James uses Elijah
Explain what happens when someone turns a sinner from error
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what James says to do when someone is sick, sinning or wandering?

topics.name: 1 Peter: overview
topics.description: 1 Peter is a letter from the apostle Peter to scattered strangers in Asia Minor, written to encourage them in suffering with the living hope, the example of Christ, holy conduct and humility under God.
evidence: Say who wrote 1 Peter and to whom
Name the main themes: hope, holiness, suffering and humility
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say how 1 Peter encourages believers who suffer?

topics.name: Born again to a living hope
topics.description: Peter blesses God who by the resurrection of Jesus has given new birth to a living hope and an inheritance kept in heaven, while faith is tested like gold and the prophets searched out this salvation.
evidence: Describe the inheritance in 1:4
Explain why trials test faith in 1:6-7
Say what the prophets searched into in 1:10-11
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what living hope Peter says believers have and why they can rejoice in trials?

topics.name: Be holy: redeemed by precious blood
topics.description: Peter calls believers to be holy as God is holy, reminds them they were redeemed by the precious blood of Christ the lamb without blemish, and says they were born again by the abiding word.
evidence: Say what Peter says redeemed them and what it was not
Explain the call to be holy in 1:15-16
Describe what the word of the Lord does according to 1:23-25
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Peter says paid the price for believers, and how they should live because of it?

topics.name: The living stone and the holy priesthood
topics.description: Peter calls Christ the living stone chosen by God, says believers are built up as a spiritual house and royal priesthood, and says they were once not a people but are now the people of God.
evidence: Explain the stone picture in 2:4-8
List the names Peter gives believers in 2:9
Say what 2:10 says changed for them
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name three things Peter calls believers in 1 Peter 2:9?

topics.name: Strangers and pilgrims: honourable conduct and submission
topics.description: Peter tells believers living as pilgrims among Gentiles to keep honest conduct, submit to rulers and honour all, and servants to be subject to masters even when treated wrongly.
evidence: Say why Peter tells them to keep honest conduct among the Gentiles
Describe how Peter says to treat the king and all men
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say how Peter says believers should behave under authorities?

topics.name: Christ suffered for us, an example
topics.description: Peter says believers are called to follow the steps of Christ, who did not sin, did not revile in return, bore our sins on the tree, and brings the strayed sheep back to the Shepherd.
evidence: Describe how Christ responded when reviled
Say what Christ did on the tree in 2:24
Explain the sheep and Shepherd picture
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain both what Christ did for us and what example he left in 1 Peter 2:21-25?

topics.name: Wives, husbands and the hidden person of the heart
topics.description: Peter addresses wives with the example of Sarah and holy women, stressing a meek and quiet spirit as precious to God, and tells husbands to live with their wives with understanding and honour as fellow heirs of the grace of life.
evidence: Say what Peter calls the adorning of great price
Describe what husbands are told in 3:7
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Peter tells husbands and wives in 1 Peter 3:1-7?

topics.name: Blessing, good conscience and suffering for doing good
topics.description: Peter tells all to be of one mind and repay evil with blessing, says suffering for righteousness is blessed, and that believers should always be ready to give a reason for their hope with meekness and a good conscience.
evidence: Say how Peter tells believers to answer evil
Explain what being ready to answer for hope looks like in 3:15
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Peter says to respond when others speak evil of us?

topics.name: Christ suffered once, the days of Noah and baptism
topics.description: Peter says Christ suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, to bring us to God, and was made alive; he mentions the spirits who were disobedient in the days of Noah, the eight saved by water, and says baptism saves by the resurrection of Jesus, who is now at God's right hand.
evidence: Say why Christ suffered once according to 3:18
Retell what 3:20 says about Noah and the eight saved through water
State where Christ is now according to 3:22
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Peter 3:18-22 says about Christ and about Noah?

topics.name: Living to the will of God
topics.description: Peter says believers who have the mind of Christ in suffering should end the old life of Gentile excess, live to God, and prepare for the end by prayer, fervent love, hospitality and using gifts for God's glory.
evidence: Describe the old life Peter says to leave behind
List the commands in 4:7-11
Explain why gifts are to be used for God's glory
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list how Peter says to live because the end of all things is at hand?

topics.name: The fiery trial and suffering as a Christian
topics.description: Peter says not to be surprised by fiery trial but to rejoice in sharing Christ's sufferings, not to suffer as an evildoer, and to entrust the soul to a faithful Creator while judgment begins at the house of God.
evidence: Say how Peter tells believers to view fiery trials
Distinguish suffering as a Christian from suffering as an evildoer
Say whom believers entrust their souls to in 4:19
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says not to be surprised by a fiery trial?

topics.name: Shepherd the flock, humility and the roaring lion
topics.description: Peter exhorts elders to shepherd willingly as examples with the chief Shepherd coming, tells all to be clothed with humility, cast cares on God, resist the devil who prowls like a roaring lion, and ends with greetings from Babylon.
evidence: Describe how elders are to lead in 5:2-3
Say what Peter tells believers to do with their cares
Say how Peter describes the devil and how to resist him
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe what Peter tells elders and everyone else to do in chapter 5?

topics.name: 2 Peter: overview
topics.description: 2 Peter is a letter from Simon Peter urging growth in the knowledge of Christ, warning against false teachers and scoffers, and pointing to the certain day of the Lord and new heavens and a new earth.
evidence: Name the three sections: growth, false teachers, the day of the Lord
Say what Peter wants believers to remember
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what 2 Peter warns about and what it tells believers to do?

topics.name: Precious promises and growing in godliness
topics.description: Peter says God has given all that pertains to life and godliness and great promises, and tells believers to add virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness and charity to faith so they are fruitful and make their calling sure.
evidence: List the qualities to add to faith in 1:5-7
Say what Peter says God has given in 1:3-4
Explain what lacking these things means in 1:9
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} list the qualities Peter says to add to faith?

topics.name: Eyewitnesses and the sure word of prophecy
topics.description: Peter says he will remind believers before his death, that the apostles were eyewitnesses of Christ's majesty when the Father's voice spoke on the holy mount, and that prophecy of scripture came from men moved by the Holy Ghost.
evidence: Say what the apostles saw and heard on the holy mount
Explain where Peter says prophecy of scripture came from
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says the apostles did not follow cunningly devised fables?

topics.name: False teachers and the examples of judgment
topics.description: Peter warns that false teachers will bring in destructive heresies out of covetousness, and shows that God judged sinning angels, the old world in Noah's day, and Sodom and Gomorrah while delivering Noah and Lot.
evidence: Describe what the false teachers do and why
List the three examples of judgment in 2:4-6
Say who God delivered in 2:5-9
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what examples Peter uses to show God judges the ungodly and rescues the godly?

topics.name: The character and end of the false teachers
topics.description: Peter describes the false teachers as presumptuous, greedy and following Balaam, promising freedom while enslaved to corruption, and says to return to the way of righteousness after knowing it is worse than never knowing it.
evidence: Name the charges in 2:13-15
Explain the saying about the dog and the sow in 2:22
Say who Peter compares them to in 2:15-16
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Peter portrays the false teachers and why turning back is so serious?

topics.name: Scoffers and the longsuffering of the Lord
topics.description: Peter says scoffers will ask where the promised coming is, recalls that the world once perished by water and the present heavens and earth are kept for fire, and says the Lord delays because he is longsuffering, not willing that any perish.
evidence: Say what the scoffers claim in 3:4
Explain what Peter says they forget in 3:5-7
Say why the Lord has not yet come, according to 3:9
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says the Lord seems slow to keep his promise?

topics.name: The day of the Lord and new heavens and earth
topics.description: Peter says the day of the Lord will come like a thief with fire dissolving the heavens and the elements, so believers should live in holiness and look for new heavens and a new earth where righteousness dwells, and grow in grace.
evidence: Describe how the day of the Lord comes
Say what kind of people Peter says we ought to be in 3:11
Say what new thing believers look for in 3:13
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say how Peter tells believers to live while they wait for the day of the Lord?

topics.name: 1 John: overview
topics.description: 1 John is a letter written so that believers may have fellowship with the Father and the Son, know they have eternal life, walk in the light, love one another, and hold to the truth that Jesus is the Christ come in the flesh.
evidence: Name the main themes: light, love, truth about Jesus, assurance
Say what John says he wrote so that in 5:13
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what 1 John wants believers to know?

topics.name: Fellowship, walking in the light and confessing sin
topics.description: John declares the Word of life that he has heard, seen and touched, says God is light, and teaches that walking in the light brings cleansing by the blood of Jesus and that confessed sins are forgiven.
evidence: Say what John says he saw and heard
Explain what God is according to 1:5
Describe what happens when we confess sins in 1:9
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what John says to do when we sin?

topics.name: Our advocate and keeping his commandments
topics.description: John writes that we may not sin, but if anyone sins we have an advocate, Jesus Christ the righteous, the propitiation for our sins and the whole world, and that knowing him is shown by keeping his commandments.
evidence: Name what Jesus is called in 2:1-2
Say how we know that we know him
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say who our advocate is and how we know we know him?

topics.name: The old and new commandment: light and hatred
topics.description: John says the commandment to love is old and yet new because the true light shines, and that hating a brother means walking in darkness while loving a brother abides in the light.
evidence: Contrast loving and hating a brother in light and darkness
Say who John addresses in 2:12-14
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how John connects loving a brother with being in the light?

topics.name: Not loving the world, and antichrists
topics.description: John tells believers not to love the world, since its lust of the flesh, lust of the eyes and pride of life pass away, and warns of many antichrists who went out from them, while the anointing from the Holy One teaches them.
evidence: List what John says is in the world
Say who John calls antichrist in 2:22
Describe what he says about those who left in 2:19
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what John says about the world and about those who deny the Son?

topics.name: Abiding in him and being children of God
topics.description: John urges abiding in Christ with confidence at his appearing, says we are now sons of God and shall be like him, and that Christ appeared to take away sins and destroy the works of the devil.
evidence: Say what we shall be when he appears
Explain why the Son of God was manifested according to 3:8
Contrast the children of God with the children of the devil
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what John says about being God's children now and later?

topics.name: Love in deed and truth, assurance and the commandment
topics.description: John says love is the message from the beginning, unlike Cain who killed his brother, that Christ laid down his life for us so we ought to love in deed and truth, and that God is greater than a condemning heart.
evidence: Say how John contrasts Cain with the love Christ showed
Explain what loving in deed and truth means in 3:17-18
State the commandment in 3:23
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what John means by loving not in word only but in deed and in truth?

topics.name: Testing the spirits
topics.description: John tells believers to test every spirit, says the spirit of God confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh, and says those in them have overcome because greater is he that is in them than he that is in the world.
evidence: Say how to test a spirit according to 4:2-3
Explain why believers have overcome in 4:4
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say how John tells us to test what teachers say?

topics.name: God is love
topics.description: John says love is of God and God is love, shown when God sent his only Son as propitiation, that we love because he first loved us, and that perfect love casts out fear and one who hates a brother cannot love God.
evidence: Say how God showed his love in 4:9-10
Explain 4:19
Describe what John says about loving God and hating a brother
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how John says we know that God is love?

topics.name: Born of God, overcoming and the witness to the Son
topics.description: John says everyone who believes Jesus is the Christ is born of God and overcomes the world through faith, and the witness of God about his Son is that God gave eternal life in the Son.
evidence: Say what overcomes the world in 5:4
State the record God gave in 5:11
Say what 5:12 says about having the Son
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what John says is the witness God gave about his Son?

topics.name: Assurance, prayer and keeping from idols
topics.description: John says he wrote so believers may know they have eternal life, that God hears prayer according to his will, mentions sin not unto death and sin unto death, and ends by telling them to keep from idols.
evidence: Say why John wrote this letter according to 5:13
Describe the confidence in prayer in 5:14-15
State John's last command
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what John wants his readers to know about eternal life and prayer?

topics.name: 2 John: overview
topics.description: 2 John is a short letter from the elder to an elect lady and her children, about walking in truth and love and not receiving those who do not bring the doctrine of Christ.
evidence: Say who writes and who receives 2 John
Name its two concerns: love and truth
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what 2 John tells believers about truth and love?

topics.name: Walk in truth and love; beware of deceivers
topics.description: The elder rejoices that the children walk in truth, repeats the commandment to love, warns of deceivers who deny Jesus Christ has come in the flesh, and says not to receive those who bring no such doctrine.
evidence: Say what the commandment from the beginning is in 2JN 1:5-6
Describe the deceivers in 2JN 1:7
Say what the elder says to do about visitors without the doctrine
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why 2 John says to love and also to be careful about false teachers?

topics.name: 3 John: overview
topics.description: 3 John is a short letter from the elder to Gaius commending his hospitality to travelling brothers, naming Diotrephes who refuses them and Demetrius who has a good report.
evidence: Name the three people the elder mentions
Say what 3 John praises
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say who Gaius, Diotrephes and Demetrius are in 3 John?

topics.name: Gaius, Diotrephes and Demetrius: hospitality and truth
topics.description: The elder commends Gaius for faithfully helping brothers and strangers who went out for Christ's name, contrasts Diotrephes who loves preeminence and rejects them, and says to imitate good and not evil, with Demetrius well reported.
evidence: Say what Gaius does that the elder praises
Describe what Diotrephes does
Say why the elder says we should receive such travellers
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} contrast what Gaius does with what Diotrephes does?

topics.name: Jude: overview
topics.description: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, urges believers to contend for the faith once delivered, warns of ungodly men who crept in, recalls examples of judgment, and ends with a call to keep in God's love and a doxology.
evidence: Say who wrote Jude
Say what Jude urges in verse 3
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Jude asks believers to contend for?

topics.name: Contend for the faith once delivered
topics.description: Jude says he had to urge believers to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints because ungodly men had crept in who turn grace into licence and deny the Lord.
evidence: Say who Jude addresses in verse 1
Describe the men in verse 4
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Jude says he had to write about contending for the faith?

topics.name: Examples of judgment: unbelievers, angels and Sodom
topics.description: Jude recalls that the Lord destroyed those who did not believe after saving a people out of Egypt, that angels who left their place are kept in chains until judgment, and that Sodom and Gomorrha suffer the vengeance of eternal fire.
evidence: List the three examples in verses 5-7
Say what Sodom and Gomorrha are set forth as
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name the three examples of judgment Jude gives?

topics.name: The ungodly men described: Cain, Balaam, Core and Enoch's prophecy
topics.description: Jude says these dreamers despise authority, have gone in the way of Cain, the error of Balaam and the rebellion of Core, are like waterless clouds and fruitless trees, and that Enoch prophesied the Lord comes to judge the ungodly.
evidence: Say what Jude says about Michael in verse 9
Name the three figures in verse 11
Describe the pictures from nature in verses 12-13
Say what Enoch prophesied in verses 14-15
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the false men in Jude using the examples and pictures Jude gives?

topics.name: Keep yourselves in the love of God and the doxology
topics.description: Jude reminds believers of the apostles' warning about mockers, tells them to build themselves up in faith, pray in the Holy Ghost, keep in God's love and show mercy to doubters, and ends praising him who is able to keep them from falling.
evidence: List Jude's commands in verses 20-23
Say who is able to keep them from falling
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say how Jude tells believers to keep themselves and whom he praises?

topics.name: Revelation: overview
topics.description: Revelation is the revelation of Jesus Christ given to John on Patmos: letters to seven churches, a vision of the throne in heaven, the Lamb, series of seals, trumpets and bowls, and the end in the new Jerusalem.
evidence: Say who gave the revelation and to whom
Name the main parts: churches, throne, Lamb, judgments, new heaven and earth
Say what is promised to the one who reads and keeps it in 1:3
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} outline the main parts of Revelation as the book itself presents them?

topics.name: Prologue: the revelation of Jesus Christ
topics.description: John introduces the revelation Jesus Christ gave, blesses those who read, hear and keep it, greets the seven churches from the God who is, was and is to come and from Jesus Christ, and announces that he cometh with clouds.
evidence: Say who is the source of the revelation in 1:1
Name what Jesus is called in 1:5
Describe what 1:7 says about his coming
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say how Revelation introduces itself and who Jesus is in these verses?

topics.name: John's vision of Christ among the lampstands
topics.description: John on Patmos hears a voice and sees one like the Son of man among seven golden candlesticks, with eyes like fire and a two-edged sword from his mouth, who says he is first and last, alive for evermore, holding the keys of death and hell.
evidence: Describe what John saw
Say what Christ says about himself in 1:17-18
Say what the seven stars and seven candlesticks are in 1:20
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the vision of Christ in Revelation 1 and what he says to John?

topics.name: Letter to Ephesus: leaving the first love
topics.description: Christ commends Ephesus for works, patience and testing false apostles, but says they have left their first love and must repent; to the one who overcomes he promises the tree of life.
evidence: Say what Christ commends and what he has against Ephesus
State the promise to the one who overcomes
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Christ praises and corrects in the church at Ephesus?

topics.name: Letter to Smyrna: faithful unto death
topics.description: Christ, who was dead and is alive, tells poor but rich Smyrna not to fear coming suffering, to be faithful unto death, and promises the crown of life and no hurt from the second death.
evidence: Say what Christ says not to fear
State the promise in 2:10-11
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Christ promises to the faithful at Smyrna?

topics.name: Letter to Pergamos: holding fast, yet holding false teaching
topics.description: Christ commends Pergamos for holding his name even where Satan dwells and where Antipas was killed, but rebukes them for holding the teaching of Balaam and of the Nicolaitanes, and calls them to repent.
evidence: Say what Pergamos did well
Name the wrong teachings Christ names
State the promise in 2:17
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Christ commends and rebukes at Pergamos?

topics.name: Letter to Thyatira: Jezebel and holding fast
topics.description: Christ commends Thyatira's love, service, faith and patience, rebukes them for tolerating Jezebel who teaches fornication and idol food, and tells the rest to hold fast until he comes, promising power over nations and the morning star.
evidence: Say what Christ commends in 2:19
Describe the charge in 2:20
State the promise in 2:26-28
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Christ says about Jezebel and about those who did not follow her?

topics.name: Letter to Sardis: a name that thou livest, and art dead
topics.description: Christ tells Sardis that they have a name for being alive but are dead, calls them to watch and repent, notes a few who have not defiled their garments, and promises white raiment and his confession of the name of the one who overcomes.
evidence: Say what Christ says about Sardis' reputation
Describe the promise in 3:4-5
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Christ says to the church at Sardis and what he promises to the few?

topics.name: Letter to Philadelphia: the open door
topics.description: Christ, holy and true, holding the key of David, tells Philadelphia he has set before them an open door, they kept his word, he will keep them from the hour of temptation, and the overcomer will be a pillar in his temple with the name of the new Jerusalem.
evidence: Describe what Christ has set before Philadelphia
State the promise to the one who overcomes in 3:12
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what Christ commends and promises to the church at Philadelphia?

topics.name: Letter to Laodicea: lukewarm, and Christ at the door
topics.description: Christ rebukes Laodicea for being neither cold nor hot and for saying they are rich while they are wretched, counsels them to buy gold, white raiment and eyesalve from him, and says he stands at the door and knocks.
evidence: Describe what Laodicea thinks of itself and what Christ says they are
Explain the picture in 3:20
State the promise to the overcomer in 3:21
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Christ says to Laodicea and the invitation in 3:20?

topics.name: The throne in heaven
topics.description: John is called up through an open door and sees a throne with one sitting on it, a rainbow, twenty-four elders in white with crowns, four living creatures crying holy, holy, holy, and all worship God as Creator.
evidence: Describe what surrounds the throne
Say what the four beasts and the elders say and do
Say why God is worthy according to 4:11
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the throne room scene and what the worshippers say?

topics.name: The sealed scroll and the Lamb
topics.description: John weeps that no one can open the sealed scroll until the Lion of the tribe of Juda appears as a Lamb as though slain, takes the scroll, and heaven and every creature worship him as worthy because he redeemed people from every nation by his blood.
evidence: Say why John wept and what was announced
Describe the Lamb and what he does
Say what the new song says about why he is worthy
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain who is worthy to open the scroll and why?

topics.name: The first six seals
topics.description: The Lamb opens six seals: four horsemen, the souls under the altar crying how long, and a great earthquake with the sun black and the moon as blood, so that people hide from the wrath of the Lamb.
evidence: List the four horses and what each rider holds or does
Describe the cry of the souls under the altar and the answer they receive
Say how the people respond to the sixth seal
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the six seals in order as John sees them?
